variant_reviews.comparison: Minimize the empirical average of K_ha(A)*(xi_hat(Z;pi_hat,mu_hat)-g_ha(A)^T beta)^2 over beta in R2, using g_ha(t)=(1,(t-a)/h) and K_ha(t)=K((t-a)/h)/h with positive h. The response is the data-dependent doubly robust pseudo-outcome computed with the supplied nuisance estimators; do not substitute the observed outcome or an appendix-only cross-fitted variant. The reported theta_hat is the intercept because g_(h,0)(0)=(1,0), not evaluation of the fitted slope at treatment zero relative to the current a. IsMinOn over all R2 expresses the optimizer predicate, while a weighted Gram inverse expression needs its nonsingularity and the kernel hypotheses giving the intended least-squares problem. No arbitrary singular inverse or unique measurable selector is supplied by the generic declarations.

Use deterministic weighted sums S_j(t)=sum_(i=1)^n (t-t_i)^j*K((t-t_i)/h_n) and response X_i. The explicit weights are K((t-t_i)/h_n)*(S2-(t-t_i)*S1)/(S2*S0-S1^2); no 1/h_n normalization appears in these sums. These are intercept weights obtained from a two-column local linear Gram system when its determinant is nonzero. Preserve the sign convention t-t_i consistently in both first moments and numerator. The source does not give a zero-denominator convention or separately state kernel mass one; real totalized division cannot silently make undefined fits zero. Negative local-linear weights are possible even with a nonnegative kernel. The separate quantile-grid endpoint issue is retained. This response and scaling differ from the pseudo-outcome fit and from multivariate variance smoothing.

At evaluation (x,z), minimize the sum of squared errors of epsilon_hat_t^2 against an intercept alpha and slope eta in R^(p+d1+d2), with regressor concatenating the UNSCALED differences X_t-x and Z_t-z and weight K1((X_t-x)/b1)*K2((Z_t-z)/b2). Take alpha_hat as the variance estimate; no clipping to positive values is specified, and a positive true variance does not guarantee a positive fitted intercept. The preceding residual formula prints unindexed X and an unindexed beta_hat inside a regime sum, unlike the earlier stacked/region coefficient conventions; retain that source dimension/index issue rather than silently repairing the response. A matrix normal-equation representation needs a correctly specified ambient dimension and invertible local Gram matrix or a chosen minimizer. Shared covariates can create redundant coordinates, and the main-text source supplies no singular or nonpositive-fit convention before subsequent residual standardization.

searches.result: Finite weighted quadratic objectives, matrix normal equations and the minimum predicate provide common algebraic ingredients, but do not supply estimator existence, uniqueness or source-specific denominator conventions.
